C_process_isolation_of_hazardous_branch.reason: the only genuine fault boundary for an in-process C-level deadlock. It must cover the productive Direct lifecycle (every engine set_state/get_state/teardown/arm/preroll/stop), not just the probe.
C_process_isolation_of_hazardous_branch.design: GStreamer OUTPUT HOST: a supervised child process owning pipeline construction and every state change; the app keeps authority over session/navigation (PlaybackSessionService), PlaybackState (PlaybackService) and engine-facing policy, and never performs a GStreamer state transition in-process.

contracts.ipc_dto: request_id + generation + operation + bounded args; result = status + observed state + typed error + diagnostics reference; no unbounded payloads
contracts.commit_rollback: stage/commit/abort receipts cross the boundary; the parent never assumes acceptance without a host result (preserves the ARM transaction semantics)
contracts.supersession: generation-tagged requests; a superseded result is discarded; cancellation is prompt and does not wait for the host to become healthy
contracts.child_failure: host death maps to a typed OUTPUT_HOST_LOST; defined recovery (release device, surface error, rebuild on demand); never fake acceptance
contracts.bounded_shutdown: TERM with deadline -> SIGKILL -> reap; no orphans, no unbounded parent wait
contracts.evidence: host lifecycle journal plus all-thread stacks captured on watchdog trigger (reuses the supervisor/evidence primitives)
contracts.non_goal: does not wire DSP/processing graphs into GStreamer (section 31 unchanged)

C_process_isolation_of_hazardous_branch.acceptance: short software reproducer under external supervision (>300/s hammer plus sequential load/stop): the typefind wedge must occur INSIDE the killed host while the app stays responsive, keeps session state coherent, recovers without restart, leaks no host processes, and shuts down within the bounded deadline; repeated cycles must show zero permanent app wedges
